$\int_0^4 6\,dx=24$ (rectangle). $\int_0^4\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx=\frac14\pi(4)^2=4\pi$ (quarter disc). $\int_0^4 x\,dx=\frac12\cdot4\cdot4=8$ (triangle).

$\int_{-2}^{4}3\,dx=3\cdot6=18$ (rectangle).
$\int_{-2}^{4}x\,dx=\frac12\cdot4\cdot4-\frac12\cdot2\cdot2=8-2=6$ (triangle above minus triangle below).

original.question: Evaluate $\int_{-3}^{3} \left(x + \sqrt{9 - x^{2}}\right)\,dx$ using Theorem 5.5.4 and geometry.
original.answer:
Split into $\int_{-3}^{3}x\,dx+\int_{-3}^{3}\sqrt{9-x^2}\,dx$.
The first is $0$: the triangles above and below the axis have equal area and cancel.
The second is the area of the upper half disc of radius $3$: $\frac12\pi(3)^2=\frac{9\pi}{2}$.
So the integral equals $\frac{9\pi}{2}$.

versions.question: Use geometry to find $\int_{-4}^{4} \left(x - \sqrt{16 - x^{2}} + 4\right)\,dx$.
versions.answer:
Split into $\int_{-4}^{4}4\,dx+\int_{-4}^{4}x\,dx-\int_{-4}^{4}\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx$.
$\int_{-4}^{4}4\,dx=4\cdot8=32$. $\int_{-4}^{4}x\,dx=0$ (equal triangles cancel). $\int_{-4}^{4}\sqrt{16-x^2}\,dx=\frac12\pi(4)^2=8\pi$.
So the integral is $32+0-8\pi=32-8\pi$.
